the malaria parasite induces stress in the body of infected patients.

the level of stress induced malaria parasite is correspond to the severity of the infection and age differences.

estimation of level of stress induces and effect of anti-malaria drugs on stress index of uncomplicated acute malaria infection.
the effect of anti malaria drug treatment in malaria infected patients.
the effect of anti-malaria drugs on stress index, lipid profile and glucose level of uncomplicated acute malaria infection in adult individuals.

malaria infection causes oxidative stress and this stress can be reduced using anti-malaria drug.

the stress index in malaria infection is corresponded to age differences and severity of infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of stress induced in uncomplicated malaria infection was higher in the older age group than younger age group.
, there is a significant difference in stress induced by malaria infection and age differences.

, there is a significant difference (p<0.05) in the level of stress induced in malaria infection in age group A (15 – 24 years), B (25 – 34 years) and C (45 – 64 years) compared to age group D (35 – 44 years).

the malaria parasite is capable of inducing oxidative stress in the host and this is reflected in the level of stress index, MDA and glucose.
